# GoPatina

> GoPatina is an open-source Go toolchain front end in which ordinary Go code can opt into running the way Rust code does: no garbage collector, ownership and borrowing, and Rust-grade memory safety. Without a flag it runs the installed Go toolchain unchanged. It is an experiment by Pigfox to get Go developers past Rust's learning curve.

Status: early. Phase 1 works for a defined subset of Go; real programs need features still in progress. Default mode works for all Go. For the phase 1 subset (functions, structs and methods, slices, strings, errors, fmt printing, and read-only s[i:] suffix arguments), -emit-rust, -patina, -patina=check, -explain and gopatina verify are implemented, checked by differential tests (92 golden programs, 24 rejection fixtures and 3 Go-only semantics cases; same stdout, first stderr line and exit status as go build) and byte-identical rebuilds. Not supported yet: goroutines and channels, maps, closures, interfaces, generics, defer, general slicing, slices with high or max bounds, saved slice views, most of the standard library. Speed goal: identical to equivalent hand-written Rust on every benchmark, meaning equivalent within ±0.5% at 5 sigma (a goal, not a claim). No official test-server run yet. Latest local measurement (2026-11-21, commit 6cb858f, laptop under load, CPU counters enabled, 300 interleaved runs, TOST at ±1% and 5 sigma): fib and suffix-sum execute the same instructions as hand-written Rust to within 0.0003%; sieve executed 1.30x the instructions and was about 7% slower (one extra bounds check per inner-loop pass); RFC 0006 loop specialization has since removed that check, so its hot loop compiles to the same machine code as the hand-written Rust; a new speed measurement is pending. Details in BENCHMARKS.md. Last updated 2026-11-21.

## Docs

- [This page as Markdown](https://gopatina.org/index.md): mission, the three build modes, how it works, roadmap, quality and benchmark policy, FAQ
- [README](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina#readme): project overview, status and quick start
- [Examples](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/EXAMPLES.md): the three build modes on three small programs, with real and planned output labelled
- [Phase 1 subset](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/patina-subset.md): the Go the patina modes accept today
- [Feature matrix](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/compat.md): supported and planned Go features
- [Go-Rust disconnects](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/go-rust-disconnects.md): where Go and Rust semantics differ
- [RFC 0001](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0001-gopatina.md): the design, the GoPatina borrow checker, Rust underneath, deployment
- [RFC 0002](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0002-concurrency.md): goroutines on a multi-threaded async runtime
- [RFC 0003](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0003-toolchain-compatibility.md): toolchain compatibility and versioning
- [RFC 0004](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0004-read-only-slice-suffix.md): read-only slice suffix arguments
- [RFC 0005](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0005-phase1-semantic-exactness.md): phase 1 semantic exactness fixes
- [Benchmarks](https://github.com/pigfox/gopatina/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md): local measurements with raw results and caveats; official results will be published there (none yet)
